title: Roasted Tomato Soup
subtitle: Deep, sweet tomato soup from the oven
excerpt: Roasting the tomatoes and onions in the oven before blending concentrates the sugars and gives this soup a depth that raw or tinned tomatoes alone cannot match. It takes longer than a quick hob soup but the flavour is worth it.
sourceNotes: Roasting tomatoes before blending is a technique used across Italian and British cooking. The slow caramelisation of the sugars in the oven gives the soup a natural sweetness and richness that differs from a straight blended tinned tomato soup.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen over low heat, stirring often.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use two large roasting tins side by side.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate.

content.text: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. Out-of-season tomatoes still work but will give a thinner flavour. The cherry tomatoes add sweetness and the balsamic vinegar deepens the overall taste.
Put all the tomatoes, the garlic halves, and the onion in the roasting tin. Drizzle with olive oil and season generously.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes until the tomatoes are collapsed and slightly charred at the edges.
Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skin into the blender. Add all the roasted tomatoes and onions, including all the juices.
Add the basil, stock, and balsamic vinegar. Blend until smooth.
Pass through a sieve if you want a very smooth soup, or serve as it is. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Reheat gently if needed. Serve with crusty bread.

items.cause: Tomatoes were under-ripe or did not caramelise fully.
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar and a little more balsamic vinegar.

items.cause: Tomatoes were particularly dry after roasting.
items.fix: Add more stock a ladleful at a time until the right consistency.
